excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
<@353136597522448385>, updating `go-verkle` to this new `go-ipa` and running `go-verkle` benchmarks: https://github.com/gballet/go-verkle/pull/290

To facilitate the results to others (copy-paste from PR description):
Reg the Go benchmarks:
```
name                                        old time/op    new time/op    delta
ProofCalculation-16                            4.65s ± 1%     4.14s ± 1%  -10.88%  (p=0.008 n=5+5)
ProofVerification-16                          26.6ms ± 2%    26.4ms ± 3%     ~     (p=0.548 n=5+5)
CommitLeaves/insert/leaves/1000-16             215ms ± 1%     203ms ± 1%   -5.89%  (p=0.008 n=5+5)
CommitLeaves/insertOrdered/leaves/1000-16      238ms ± 1%     224ms ± 3%   -5.63%  (p=0.008 n=5+5)
CommitLeaves/insert/leaves/10000-16            2.46s ± 1%     2.29s ± 2%   -6.79%  (p=0.008 n=5+5)
CommitLeaves/insertOrdered/leaves/10000-16     2.50s ± 2%     2.37s ± 1%   -5.18%  (p=0.008 n=5+5)
CommitFullNode-16                             32.0ms ± 1%    30.1ms ± 1%   -5.95%  (p=0.008 n=5+5)
ModifyLeaves-16                                9.34s ± 1%     8.23s ± 1%  -11.93%  (p=0.008 n=5+5)
```
So this makes sense if we try extrapolating from my benchmarks.

Running `benchs/main.go` separate benchmaks seem to have also 1.10x speedup (in some scaled down setup). If I test the original setup (1 million pre-inserted leaves, and insert 10k leaves; I got a 5x speedup which... is quite crazy, but my bet is my machine swapping RAM (too good to be true))

Will be interesting to see what you find out running that `block-replay` benchmark. :)
